newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan seeks emergency fuel oil cargo in March.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seeks emergency fuel oil cargo in March.

text.p: Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources is seeking by tender an emergency end-March fuel oil cargo, a ministry source said on Monday.
"The tender, which was issued on February 5 is for an emergency requirement for a power station," the source said.

The spot tender which seeks 50,000 tonnes of 125-centistoke grade fuel oil with a 1.0-percent sulphur content, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keamari, closes February 17 and is expected to awarded later on Monday evening or Tuesday.
Pakistan normally buys fuel oil and other oil products by quarterly tenders.
Its next quarterly tender to buy fuel oil, diesel and motor gasoline for April-June deliveries, are expected to be issued around February 25, the source said.
In its last quarterly tender for January-March deliveries, Pakistan bought two 25,000-tonne cargoes of 125-centistoke, 1.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for February and March deliveries.

It also bought two 50,000-tonne cargoes of 125-centistoke, 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil each month between January and March and one 40,000-tonne cargo of the same grade a month during the same period.
All the fuel oil cargoes were purchased from MidEast trader Bakri Trading.
